purpose: Permit paragraph evidence for an unknown role without inventing a named candidate, while preserving the complete frozen status vocabulary.

contract.proposed: candidate_id must be a supplied speaker/person cue alias; evidence_ids must be nonempty supplied paragraph or cue aliases; target_ids must be supplied paragraph aliases.
contract.unknown: candidate_id must be null; evidence_ids may be empty or contain only supplied paragraph aliases; target_ids must be supplied paragraph aliases.
contract.mixed: Preserves v1's permissive candidate/evidence shape; any non-null candidate and every evidence alias must bind to supplied cue/evidence spans.
contract.needs_review: Preserves v1's permissive candidate/evidence shape; any non-null candidate and every evidence alias must bind to supplied cue/evidence spans.
contract.all_statuses: Role and status must belong to the frozen request vocabulary. The generic schema checks status-dependent shape; host validation binds aliases and controlled values to the exact frozen request.

speaker_roles.basis: The paragraph is a speaking turn, but the supplied passage contains no supported speaker identity.

validation_layers.transport_schema: Constrains the four frozen status values, proposed and unknown relationships, and paragraph-shaped target aliases. Mixed and needs_review retain v1's permissive shape.
validation_layers.host_validation: Binds aliases and role/status values to the exact frozen request. Candidate aliases must be supplied speaker/person cues; evidence aliases must be supplied evidence spans, with paragraph-only evidence for unknown.

compatibility: Version 1 schemas, prompts, run stores and comparison results remain unchanged. This v2.1 correction preserves v1 mixed/needs_review shape semantics; it changes neither canonical labels nor human decisions.

revalidation.scope: Four exact saved replies from the Mini/Qwen two-case comparison, validated against their frozen provider inputs without provider calls.
revalidation.interpretation: Qwen's unknown attribution with paragraph evidence is structurally valid under v2. Mini's two proposed person-mention rows with null candidates remain invalid; no partial salvage. Structural validity is not semantic correctness or human approval.
